$comment: Machine-readable form of TASK.md. Prefer this to parsing prose. The prize is deliberately absent: anyone may add to a bounty, so it is mutable and lives on the platform, not in a pinned repository file.
title: The Cramér–Wold theorem, in Lean
$comment_criteria: The commit the posted task pins. What counts as a solution was fixed here and cannot move; the statement below is compared against this commit, not against main.
$comment_locked: Everything from the top of the statement file through the ':= by' opening the proof — imports, namespace, open, variable and the theorem signature — must be identical to the criteria commit. Comments and blank lines are ignored. Adding a hypothesis is a different theorem, not a partial solution.

winConditions.$comment_forbidden: Enforced via the axiom report rather than by text search: a sorry anywhere beneath the theorem appears as sorryAx transitively, and native_decide appears as Lean.ofReduceBool.

$comment_protected: These define the task or judge it. A submission that modifies any of them is rejected without further review.
$comment_preflight: Checks tools, free disk, network, API key and GitHub access. Run before anything else; exits non-zero if something would block you.
$comment_selfCheck: The identical script CI runs. Exit code 0 means the automated side of the review will pass.

prerequisites.$comment: The Mathlib build cache unpacks to about 7.4 GB under .lake/. Insufficient disk is the most common non-mathematical cause of failure.

$comment_setup: cache get is not optional — without it Lean compiles Mathlib from source.

steps: Fork the repository and close the sorry on a branch.
Open a pull request against math-market/cramer-wold.
Submit the pull request URL as your solution on taskUrl.
submission.$comment_license: Settled submissions are archived and republished as part of a permanent public record, so the artifact must be licensed to permit that.
submission.$comment_credentials: During the beta, platform API keys are provisioned by a human. An automated solver without a key should stop once verify.sh passes and report that a verified proof is ready.
